name: browserwright
label: browserwright (your Chrome)
_note: browserwright >= 0.9.0 has a native one-shot markdown command that owns its
whole lifecycle: it creates a throwaway session, navigates, converts, and
tears the session down. Verified 2026-08-09: no leaked sessions afterwards.
--backend defaults to `extension`, the user's real Chrome, which is what we
want: the isolated cdp backend would launch a new Chrome and steal the macOS
active window. Do-not-disturb outranks isolation. It also means this rung
carries the user's login state, which is the whole reason it is worth having.
--max-chars=0 disables its 8000-char print cap. Measured: a Wikipedia article
comes through stdout at 46,033 bytes, so the ~10KB executor stdout truncation
that forced the old wrapper script does not apply on this path.
--mode defaults to `auto`: extract the main content, and fall back to the
page minus nav/aside/footer if extraction collapses. Switch to --mode=full
here if a docs or API-reference page ever comes back missing its tables or
code blocks — that is readability's known weak spot, and `full` keeps every
link.
failWhen.matches: [] switches OFF the core default list, and the probe on
2026-08-09 says keep it that way: every case that returned content returned
genuine content, including x.com, where this rung got a real logged-in
profile view (2199 chars) that an anonymous fetch is refused.
This is the ONLY fetch rung this package ships, so a false rejection here
fails the whole call rather than dropping to something else. That asymmetry
is why the bar for rejecting is deliberately high. Drop your own provider
JSON into this directory to add a cheaper or anonymous rung ahead of it.
Observed but deliberately accepted: g2.com returns a 1330-char skip-links
stub after 62 seconds — thin, and uncomfortably close to the 90s timeout.
Known upstream bug (2026-08-09): a PDF URL exits 3 with a raw
`TargetClosedError` traceback, not the documented UnsupportedContentType
refusal, so the chain trace carries a Playwright stack instead of a sentence.

retries/retryWhen: measured 2026-08-09, PageBindTimeout ('timed out binding Playwright to session target ... no replacement page was created') fires intermittently on a healthy daemon and the CLI itself marks it retryable:true. With one rung per tool there is nothing to fall through to, so one retry here is the difference between a blip and a failed call. Scoped by retryWhen so a 404 or an auth wall is not retried.
